---

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**

A person who saves articles to a reading list can only look at that list inside the
product. Nothing lets them take the list away, so the weekly review they actually do
happens against a screen they cannot annotate, file, or keep. Two separate requests
asked for the same way out of this — a Markdown file of the saved list.

**Who is affected?**

- **Someone who saves articles and reviews them weekly.** Today they review from the
  screen; they want a file they can keep alongside the rest of their weekly notes.
  Every request in this group came from Max Adamsky in that role.

**What exists today?**

A saved reading list exists and can be read on screen. [ASSUMPTION] No export or
download of it exists — that is what both source requests ask to add.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**

- Producing a Markdown file of the saved reading list that the person can keep.
- Showing, for each entry, the date the article was saved.
- Showing, for each entry, a link back to the article itself.
- Saying plainly when there is nothing to export, rather than handing over an empty
  or broken file.

**Out of Scope:**

- Narrowing the reading list to one topic. This was request MAX-29, left in the
  triage inbox and not shaped here.
- Remembering the reader's chosen text size. This was request MAX-30, likewise left
  in the triage inbox.
- Any format other than Markdown. Neither source request asked for one.
- Changing what saving an article does, or what the reading list holds.

---

## 3. Units of Work

- **Unit 1 (Urgent): Export the saved reading list as a Markdown file.** A person
  can take their saved reading list out of the product as one Markdown file and keep
  it with their weekly notes, which today they cannot do at all.
- **Unit 2 (High): Show each article's saved date and a link back to it.** A person
  reading the exported file can tell when each article was saved and can open the
  article itself from the file, instead of holding a list of bare titles.
- **Unit 3 (Medium): Say plainly when there is nothing to export.** A person whose
  reading list is empty, or whose list cannot be read, is told so directly instead of
  receiving a file that looks complete and is not.

**Happy path:** the person asks for the export → the saved list is read → each saved
article becomes an entry carrying its saved date and its link → one Markdown file is
handed back → the person keeps it for the weekly review.

---

## 4. Requirements

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | Produce a Markdown file containing the saved reading list | Urgent | For a reading list holding N saved articles, the exported file holds N entries and is valid Markdown. |
| FR-002 | Each entry identifies its article | Urgent | Every entry names the article it came from; no entry is blank or unattributed. |
| FR-003 | Each entry shows the date the article was saved | High | For an article saved on a known date, that date appears on its entry; an entry whose saved date is unknown says so rather than showing a guessed or blank date. |
| FR-004 | Each entry carries a link back to the article | High | Every entry carries a link that resolves to the article it names; an article with no recorded link says so on its entry rather than carrying a broken one. |
| FR-005 | An empty or unreadable list produces a plain message, not a file that looks complete | Medium | For an empty reading list, the person is told the list is empty and no entries are produced. For a list that cannot be read, the person is told that, and no partial file is presented as complete. |

**Design-system components:** not applicable — config records ui_facing: false.

**Key constraints:**

- Markdown is the only output format either source request asked for.
- The export reads the saved reading list; it never changes it.

      being reviewed? MAX-27 says weekly reading list, MAX-28 says the saved reading
      list without qualification. Owner: Max Adamsky.

- [ ] What starts the export, and where does the resulting file go? Owner: Max Adamsky.
- [ ] In what order do entries appear — most recently saved first, or the order they
